questionsToConsider: Which decision are you about to make, such as episode length, a new format or release day? Keep the questions that feed it.
Do you want to hear from brand-new listeners, or only regulars? That changes where you share the link.
Would you give listeners a reason to answer, like a shout-out on the show?
Do you need an email for anything, or can the survey stay anonymous?
guide.howToUseResponses: Compare answers from long-time listeners with first-timers: regulars tell you what to protect, newcomers tell you what hooked them. Use the length and listening-place answers together, since commuters and gym listeners often want shorter episodes. Pull the topic and guest ideas into your planning list, and read every low-rating reply, because those listeners are the ones closest to leaving.
customizeSteps: Put your show's name in the greeting and swap the formats for the ones you actually make or are thinking about.
Mention the survey link in an episode and in the show notes, since most listeners never visit your website.
Read the answers in the dashboard after a couple of weeks, and export them to CSV if you want to sort the topic ideas.

faqs.q: What questions should I ask in a podcast survey?
faqs.a: How people found the show, how and where they listen, what length and format they prefer, what they rate it, and what they want next. Leave room for their own words.

faqs.q: How do I get podcast listeners to fill out a survey?
faqs.a: Ask on the show itself and put the link in the episode notes. Saying it takes three minutes and that you'll act on it helps more than any prize.

faqs.q: Should a podcast survey ask about guests?
faqs.a: Yes, if your show has guests. Ask what listeners want to learn from a guest, not only names, so you can judge whether a suggestion fits.

faqs.q: Can listeners answer on their phone?
faqs.a: Yes. The survey runs as a chat, one question at a time, which suits people answering straight from their podcast app.
